title: Planner: local custom fields on plan tasks
summary: Hold: the low cost rating conflicts with the briefing's documented need for additional licences for field creators. The feature description, rollout information and control calls are supported; the licence-request path needs a small completion.

claims.quote: Custom Fields let you tailor your plans to match the way your team works.

claims.claim: The five field types are Text, Number, Date, Yes/No and Choice.
claims.quote: Add Text, Number, Date, Yes/No, and Choice fields to capture the information that matters most.

claims.claim: The cited pages name no meter or separate charge for custom fields.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner local custom fields licensing pricing meter separate charge; "Planner" "custom fields" "price" meter. Opened Planner service description, trial/licence assignments and Planner for admins; no custom-field meter or separate charge stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn and the notice name no admin role specific to managing local custom fields.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner" "custom fields" "role" permissions; Planner local custom fields admin documentation role permissions text field maximum characters. Opened Planner for admins and customFieldDefinition; read MC1492955. None names a custom-field-specific admin role.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide control specific to Planner custom fields is documented on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner local custom fields tenant admin disable restrict Set-PlannerConfiguration Microsoft Graph settings. Opened Planner for admins, disable-planner, manage-planner-app, customFieldDefinition and plannerPlanConfiguration-update; no field-specific tenant switch.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > Requests is the licence-request assignment route after a Planner trial.
claims.quote: Within the Requests tab, you can see all the submitted requests and assign the licenses either one at a time or in bulk. ... Select a request and then choose from an available license via the drop-down menu under Select a product.
claims.fix: Complete controls[1].ui.path as 'Billing > Licenses > Requests > request > Select a product', keeping the note that this route handles requests after a trial, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/planner/understand-planner-trial-and-license-assignments.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense assigns user licences using addLicenses to specify the SKU.
claims.quote: POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense ... addLicenses ... objects that specify the licenses to add. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/assignLicense ... "skuId"

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches audit search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog searches audit records and runs in Exchange Online PowerShell, rather than restricting fields.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. ... You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Searching in the Purview portal requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role there.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.claim: The audit-search cmdlet needs the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.
claims.quote: To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block turns off the Planner app in Teams.
claims.quote: In the left pane of the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false is the documented organisation-level Planner disable call.
claims.quote: Turn off Planner for your organization using PowerShell ... Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false

claims.claim: The Planner disable PowerShell instructions are for a global admin.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell.

claims.claim: The Teams Block action governs the Planner app in Teams, not a custom-field-specific setting.
claims.quote: You can turn off or turn on the app at the org level on the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The PowerShell disable page covers basic plans in Teams and Web and all plans in other Planner endpoints.
claims.quote: This article applies to: ... Basic plans in the Planner app in Teams and Web ... All plans in other Planner endpoints (including Planner mobile, and Planner connectors).

claims.claim: The cited Planner disable and Teams app-management pages do not mention custom fields.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner local custom fields tenant admin disable restrict Set-PlannerConfiguration Microsoft Graph settings. Opened and read https://learn.microsoft.com/planner/disable-planner and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-planner-app; neither mentions custom fields.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The default state is user-opt-in: users choose to add fields and no admin enablement is required.
claims.quote: This feature is optional. Existing plans are not affected unless users add Custom Fields. ... No tenant-level configuration or admin setup is required to enable Custom Fields.

claims.claim: Licensing is mixed between Microsoft 365 read-only entitlement and the qualifying licences for fuller custom-field capabilities.
claims.quote: | Feature name | Microsoft Planner Included in Microsoft 365 | Planner Plan 1 | Planner and Project Plan 3 | Microsoft 365 Copilot | ... | Local custom fields | View only | Yes | Yes | Yes |

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Cost is Low despite the rationale identifying spending on licences for users who must create fields.
claims.quote: cost: "low" ... Low. Viewing needs a Microsoft 365 licence; creating fields needs Planner Plan 1 or Planner and Project Plan 3, so spend depends on how many people must create fields.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'medium' under the scale for additional licences for a subset of users. Replace the cost rationale with 'Medium. Users who need to create fields need a qualifying licence beyond Microsoft 365 read-only access, so spend depends on how many creators need licensing.' In Cost and licensing, replace 'The indirect cost is licensing for people who need to create fields, plus the time to brief users and handle support requests.' with 'Direct costs are licences for people who need to create fields; indirect costs are the time to brief users and handle support requests.'

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses is the place to check qualifying licence assignments.
claims.quote: You can accept or deny each request using the Licenses tab located under Billing. Within the Requests tab, you can see all the submitted requests and assign the licenses either one at a time or in bulk.
claims.fix: Narrow the checklist bullet to the cited request workflow: 'Review licence requests from plan owners after a trial (Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > Requests > request > Select a product).' The cited page documents processing requests, not reviewing every existing licence holder.
